prompt: Did the LED streetlight conversion save energy and reduce crime?

sources.S1:
The city replaced 42,000 sodium streetlights with LED fixtures between 2021 and 2023. Annual electricity use for street lighting fell from 31 gigawatt-hours to 13 gigawatt-hours, and maintenance calls dropped by 40 percent.

The upgrade did not include lights in city parks.
sources.S2: Police data show reported nighttime burglaries in the retrofitted districts fell 7 percent, but daytime burglaries fell by a similar amount, so the analysts could not attribute the decline to lighting.

writer.markdown:
# Question: Did the LED streetlight conversion save energy and reduce crime?

## Answer
Street lighting electricity use dropped by more than half, from 31 to 13 gigawatt-hours [S1]. Annual street lighting use fell by 18 gigawatt-hours [S1]. Annual street lighting use fell from 31 megawatt-hours to 13 megawatt-hours [S1].

## Evidence
- About 42 thousand sodium lights were swapped for LEDs [S1].
- Maintenance calls rose by 40 percent after the upgrade [S1].
- Brighter LED lighting reduced nighttime burglaries by 7 percent [S2].
- Nighttime and daytime burglaries both fell by similar amounts [S2].

## Counter-evidence and limits
- Lights in city parks were left out of the upgrade [S1].
- The upgrade covered every streetlight in the city, including parks [S1].
- Analysts could not attribute the burglary decline to lighting [S2].
- The LED fixtures are expected to last 20 years.

## Next actions
- Compare park and street areas after dark (judgment)

## Sources
- [S1] Public works LED report
- [S2] Police burglary analysis
